Article 11

(1) The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of women's protection institutions.

(2) The Regent establishes policies, programs and activities for women's protection to eliminate all forms of discrimination and violence against women in the Region.

(3) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's protection as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.

(4) Membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) consists of relevant Regional Apparatus Work Units, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.

(5) Further provisions regarding the Establishment of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 17

Any person who intentionally commits violence against women shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.

Article 8

Women victims of violence have the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both government and non-government.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Region is Central Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Central Bangka Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities as women and as men that are created and internalized in the family, society and culture of the society in which we live including expectations, attitudes, characteristics, behavior of how to be a man and how to be a woman.
6. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that directly or indirectly is based on differentiation of humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
7. Women's empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
8. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security to women conducted by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes deprivation of a person's freedom.

10.Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.

11.Regional cooperation is an agreement between governor and governor or governor and regent/mayor or between regent/mayor and other regent/mayor, and or governor, regent/mayor with third parties, which is made in writing and gives rise to rights and obligations.

CHAPTER V

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obligated and responsible for efforts to empower women.

(2) Efforts to empower women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) In order to improve the position, role and quality of women and efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national and state life, women must be empowered.

(4) Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (3) is directed to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, order and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 10

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to women so that they can realize and enjoy a decent standard of living.

(2) Provisions regarding Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7

(1) Women have the right to receive special protection from things that threaten their safety and/or health.

(2) Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.

(3) Special protection as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of health services related to:

a. menstruation;
b. pregnancy;
c. childbirth; and
d. breastfeeding.

Article 16

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women in the Region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically starting from planning through to policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women for the current year.

(4) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.

(5) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.

(6) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women to the Governor.

(7) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (6) shall be conducted annually and/or when necessary.

Article 14

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups and community social organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of:

a. active role in policy formulation;
b. cooperation; and/or
c. complaints/reports.
(4) Procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 9

(1) Women have equal opportunities without discrimination to obtain employment.

(2) Equal opportunity as referred to in paragraph (1) is realized through the fulfillment of women's rights to receive equal treatment from employers.

(3) Employers who employ female workers must provide protection in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(4) Protection that must be provided by employers to women as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

(1) Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women in the Region shall be sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Central Bangka Regency.

(2) In the event that the Region receives funding assistance for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women from the Government, it must be carried out in accordance with the laws and regulations.

Article 8

Women victims of violence have the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both government and non-government.

Article 10

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to women so that they can realize and enjoy a decent standard of living.

(2) Provisions regarding Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 11

(1) The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of women's protection institutions.

(2) The Regent establishes policies, programs and activities for women's protection to eliminate all forms of discrimination and violence against women in the Region.

(3) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for women's protection as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.

(4) Membership of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) consists of relevant Regional Apparatus Work Units, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.

(5) Further provisions regarding the Establishment of task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:

1. Region is Central Bangka Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Central Bangka.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Central Bangka Regency.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities as women and as men that are created and internalized in the family, society and culture of the society in which we live including expectations, attitudes, characteristics, behavior of how to be a man and how to be a woman.
6. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that directly or indirectly is based on differentiation of humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
7. Women's empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capabilities, knowledge and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
8. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security to women conducted by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes deprivation of a person's freedom.

10.Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations.

Article 17

Any person who intentionally commits violence against women shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the laws and regulations.

Article 16

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women in the Region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically starting from planning through to policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women for the current year.

(4) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.

(5) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.

(6) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women to the Governor.

(7) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (6) shall be conducted annually and/or when necessary.

Article 14

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups and community social organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of:

a. active role in policy formulation;
b. cooperation; and/or
c. complaints/reports.
(4) Procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obligated and responsible for efforts to empower women.

(2) Efforts to empower women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) In order to improve the position, role and quality of women and efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national and state life, women must be empowered.

(4) Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (3) is directed to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, order and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 15

(1) Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women in the Region shall be sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Central Bangka Regency.

(2) In the event that the Region receives funding assistance for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women from the Government, it must be carried out in accordance with the laws and regulations.

Article 9

(1) Women have equal opportunities without discrimination to obtain employment.

(2) Equal opportunity as referred to in paragraph (1) is realized through the fulfillment of women's rights to receive equal treatment from employers.

(3) Employers who employ female workers must provide protection in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(4) Protection that must be provided by employers to women as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 16

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 6

(1) The Regional Government is obligated and responsible for efforts to empower women.

(3) In order to improve the position, role and quality of women and efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national and state life, women must be empowered.
